title: Moving a piece twice
line: Each move in the opening should bring out a piece that has not moved yet, unless moving again gains something.

steps.text: Each move in the opening should bring another piece into play. Here your knight and bishop are out, and so are two of Black's.
Make a move that brings another piece into the game or gets ready to castle.

wrong.f3g5: That moves the knight a second time for nothing, and the queen simply takes it.
wrong.f3h4: That moves the knight a second time for nothing, and the queen simply takes it.

steps.hint: A pawn move can open a line for your other bishop.
steps.after: A piece is out, or the king is closer to safety.

steps.text: Moving a piece again is worth it when it makes a real threat. Here Black brought out a knight instead of the bishop.
Move your knight a second time, to g5. With the bishop it attacks f7, so Black has to answer.

also.d2d3: Guarding your pawn is also sound. This lesson shows the knight move.

steps.after: Black blocks the bishop with a pawn.

steps.text: Take the pawn on d5. You are a pawn up for now.
steps.after: Now Black's knight moves a second time, to attack your bishop. That is worth it too: it gains time.

steps.text: Move the bishop away with check, so Black must spend its next move on the check.
steps.after: Each side moved a piece again only to make a threat. Without a threat, a second move by the same piece is a lost move.

summary: A piece that moves twice in the opening costs a move another piece needed. Move it again only to make a threat.
